name: MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Records
geographic_footprint: Global coverage (±88° latitude for 128 px/deg tiles; ±90° for 4 px/deg)
coverage: Near-global Mars topography from ~600M altimetry returns. Available as 16 regional tiles at 128 px/deg (MEGT*HB) and single global maps at 4 px/deg (MEGT90N000CB), 16 px/deg (MEGT90N000EB), and 32 px/deg (MEGT90N000FB)
scientific_limitations: Laser track spacing widens near equator (up to 12 km gap between tracks); vertical accuracy ~1 m on flat plains, degrading on steep slopes (>5°); reference surface is IAU 2000 sphere (R=3396.0 km or 3396.19 km) with elevations referenced to MOLA Areoid
description: Global digital elevation model of Mars produced from Mars Global Surveyor MOLA altimetry. Elevations represent height in metres relative to the Goddard Mars potential model GMM3 areoid evaluated to degree and order 50.

name: HRSC Digital Terrain Models
geographic_footprint: Regional orbital swaths and quadrangle mosaics (non-global, ~50%–70% accumulated coverage)
coverage: Regional stereo DTM swaths along elliptical orbit ground tracks; quadrangle mosaics (e.g. MC-11 Oxia Planum). Not a contiguous global dataset
scientific_limitations: Coverage is non-contiguous strip-based; vertical accuracy (10–40 m) varies with stereo convergence angle, atmospheric dust opacity, and surface texture contrast; boundary artifacts exist between adjacent orbit strips
description: High-resolution stereo-photogrammetric digital terrain models derived from Mars Express HRSC along-track stereo channels. DTMs provide regional 50–100 m/px topography referenced to the MOLA Areoid.

name: USGS SIM 3292 — Geologic Map of Mars
instrument: Multiple (MOLA, THEMIS, Viking, MOC, CTX, HRSC)
coverage: Global geologic map of Mars showing contact relations, unit descriptions, and structural features at 1:20M scale
scientific_limitations: Scale limits detail to features ≥~20 km; interpretive boundaries may differ from emerging high-resolution mapping; based on data available through ~2012
description: The first global geologic map of Mars in a digital GIS format, published by the USGS as Scientific Investigations Map 3292 (Tanaka et al., 2014). It synthesises decades of orbiter imagery and topographic data.

name: HiRISE Reduced Data Records
geographic_footprint: Targeted sites (not global); ~3% of Mars surface
coverage: Targeted high-resolution imagery of scientifically selected sites across Mars, including candidate landing sites and geologic features of interest
scientific_limitations: Sparse, non-contiguous spatial coverage; large file sizes (~1–10 GB per observation); map-projected products may have minor geometric distortions at steep slopes
description: The highest-resolution orbital images of Mars from MRO's HiRISE camera. Individual observations cover ~5 km swath widths and are used for detailed geomorphologic analysis and landing-site characterization.

name: CTX Experiment Data Records
coverage: Broad-coverage monochrome imagery providing context for HiRISE observations; over 95% of Mars surface covered
scientific_limitations: Grayscale only (no color); individual frames require mosaicking for contiguous coverage; radiometric calibration differences between frames
description: The MRO Context Camera provides grayscale imagery at ~6 m/px, bridging the resolution gap between wide-angle imagers and HiRISE. CTX mosaics form the backbone of modern Mars base maps.

name: CRISM Targeted Reduced Data Records
instrument: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)
coverage: Visible-to-near-infrared spectral cubes identifying mineral assemblages at targeted and survey sites across Mars
scientific_limitations: Detector degradation over mission lifetime reduced spectral range; atmospheric correction required; targeted mode covers <2% of Mars surface
description: Hyperspectral imaging data from MRO CRISM used to identify and map surface minerals on Mars. Targeted observations have 544 spectral channels spanning 0.36–3.92 µm wavelengths.

name: THEMIS Infrared Image Cubes
coverage: Global daytime and nighttime infrared mosaics used for thermophysical property mapping and surface composition studies
scientific_limitations: IR bands have limited spectral resolution compared to TES; daytime images have illumination artifacts; nighttime thermal inertia depends on atmospheric corrections
description: Multi-band infrared and visible imagery from Mars Odyssey's THEMIS instrument. Global daytime IR and nighttime IR mosaics enable thermal-inertia and surface-composition mapping.

name: MSL Radiation Assessment Detector Data
geographic_footprint: Gale Crater surface (point measurements along traverse)
coverage: Continuous surface-level radiation dose-rate measurements (GCR and SEP) acquired during Curiosity rover traverse in Gale Crater
scientific_limitations: Single-point measurement at Gale Crater floor; dose rates vary with altitude and atmospheric thickness; sensor shielded by rover body in some directions
description: The first surface-level radiation measurements on Mars from the Curiosity rover's RAD instrument. Data include dose rates from galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and solar energetic particle (SEP) events, critical for human exploration planning.

name: MSL REMS Environmental Data
geographic_footprint: Gale Crater surface (point measurements along traverse)
coverage: In-situ atmospheric pressure, temperature, humidity, wind, and UV flux measurements acquired at Gale Crater
scientific_limitations: Wind sensor partially damaged during landing; humidity sensor performance degrades at low temperatures; single-site measurements not representative of global conditions
description: Environmental monitoring data from Curiosity's REMS station in Gale Crater, including atmospheric pressure, air and ground temperature, relative humidity, UV radiation, and wind speed/direction.

name: MSL Curiosity Rover Imagery
coverage: Surface imagery from Curiosity rover cameras spanning the full traverse through Gale Crater including Mount Sharp foothills
scientific_limitations: Color calibration varies between Mastcam-34 and Mastcam-100; MAHLI images have limited depth of field; NavCam/HazCam have lower spatial resolution
description: Multi-camera surface imagery from the Curiosity rover including Mastcam mosaics, MAHLI close-up images of rocks and soil, MARDI descent imagery, and engineering camera navigation images.

name: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Imagery
instrument: Mastcam-Z, SuperCam RMI, SHERLOC-WATSON, NavCam, HazCam, PIXL MCC
coverage: Surface imagery from Perseverance rover cameras spanning the traverse through Jezero Crater and its ancient river delta
scientific_limitations: Mastcam-Z zoom range introduces variable resolution; SuperCam RMI has narrow field of view; calibration target images needed for accurate color reproduction
description: Multi-camera surface imagery from the Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater including Mastcam-Z stereo panoramas, SuperCam Remote Micro-Imager context images, WATSON close-ups, and engineering camera data.
